## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In the edition of V. Fausböll, the Jātaka is positioned as the sixth story of its section, preceding the *Mahāsupinajātaka*, and opens around the canonical verse beginning *Asaṁkiyomhi gāmamhi* ("The village breeds no fear in me") [Fausböll 1877]. The framing narrative is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha recounts the episode concerning a lay follower (*upāsaka*) residing in Sāvatthi who was an earnest stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*); while journeying through a forest with a merchant caravan that had halted to establish a camp, the lay disciple calmly walked up and down at the base of a tree [Fausböll 1877].
